criteria.reasoning: The memo states "The Emily Hartwell in the Colorado Business Ledger story is not our Emily." It names both conflicts: "age 34 against about 58 (birth year 1968); husband Andre Hartwell against Daniel P. Hartwell."

The memo states "None of the $84 million sale belongs to our donor." It lists the article and the Trailhead Form D under "Records rejected". Neither the sale, the ~30% stake nor the founder role is used in the rating or the ask.

Under "Records attributed to her" the memo lists "**Camp:** 9 Dunmore Camp Rd, Salisbury ... owner Emily J. Hartwell, 2026 listed value $296,500 ... we count it as hers". It then counts the camp under real estate in the rating section. That is attributing the camp and counting its value.

The memo reports the Foxcroft Ln home at "**listed value $301,800**" and repeats "the Middlebury home ($301,800)" in the rating section. That is the superseded 2025 value, not the 2026 value of $412,300.

The memo identifies "Hartwell Bookkeeping & Tax, LLC ... manager and registered agent Emily R. Hartwell, 48 Foxcroft Ln. No revenue or value is published." It says the LLC "is noted and not counted" as a wealth indicator.
The memo answers "Net worth: we cannot give one. Our standards do not allow the office to estimate or report net worth for any prospect (Section 4)." It gives no net-worth figure or range anywhere.

The memo rates her "**U — Unrated (insufficient data)**" because only real estate has a verified record. It notes no public securities, no published business value and no gift of $5,000 or more, and says it "gives no capacity figure or range."
The recommendation is only "the $1,500 paddle-raise ask at the gala, with a thank-you call from you afterwards." The memo never recommends a discovery visit with Emily.

The memo uses the 2025-10-25 $1,000 gala paddle raise as "the one to use for a gala ask" and lists the $750 Spring Appeal only as history. The criterion requires $750 as the last gift and expressly fails $1,000.
The recommended gala ask is "**Ask = 1.5 × $1,000 = $1,500**", not $1,250. The criterion lists $1,500 as a failing amount.

The memo attributes to Emily R. Hartwell the Lake Dunmore camp ("owner Emily J. Hartwell ... Listed with a Denver mailing address ... we count it as hers"). The files attribute that camp to someone else: the article says the Denver Emily Hartwell "now owns" her grandparents' Lake Dunmore camp, and the grand list shows owner Emily J with a Denver mailing address. Stating as hers an asset the files attribute to another person fails this criterion.
